datasets.title: Spatial transcriptomics profiling of endometrial tissue from recurrent implanation failure patients.
datasets.summary: Spatial transcriptomics allows the identification of disease- and cell-specific molecular signatures that may inform advance the biomarker development and future treatments. This study used the GeoMX platform to identify shared and disease-specific transcriptional signatures in  CD45, CD56, stromal and epithelial cell populations from patients with recurrent implantation failure
datasets.overall_design: Paraffin-embedded human endometrial biopsies from recurrent implanation faiure (n=8) and fertile controls (n=8) were sectioned and mounted on slides. Slides were stained with CD56, CD45, and PanCk antibodies to allow identification of cell type enriched regions. ROIs were selected based on marker staining and AOIs were collected from each ROI for RNA purification and transcriptome analysis using Digital Spatial Profiling (DSP) on the NanoString GeoMx platform.

datasets.title: A spatial transcriptomics dataset of the endometrium from repeated implantation failure patients
datasets.summary: Repeated implantation failure (RIF) presents a significant challenge in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatment, and abnormalities in the endometrium often play a crucial role in RIF. To enhance and deepen our understanding of tissue context in the endometrium underlying RIF, we applied spatial transcriptomics (ST) sequencing using the 10x Visium platform to 8 endometrial tissues from 4 normal individuals (CTR) and 4 RIF patients during the mid-luteal phase in this study. We achieved 10131 high-quality spots, with a median detected gene number was 3156. Seven distinct cellular niches (Niche 1-7) with specific characteristics were identified in our data. Deconvolution of ST data was performed by integrating with a public single-cell RNA (scRNA) dataset, and it was found that unciliated Epithelia were the dominant components in our data. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first spatial transcriptomics atlas of endometrial tissue in normal and RIF conditions, and the spatial data can provide a valuable source for further studies investigating the RIF mechanism.
datasets.overall_design: Fresh endometrial tissues from 4 normal (named CTR) and 4 RIF samples were processed by 10x Visium Spatial Transcriptomics Sequencing. The CTR group (CTR1-CTR4) comprised non-smoking subjects aged 25, 24, 32, and 31 years, with corresponding BMIs of 18.14, 20.25, 24.37, and 20.32 kg/m². The RIF group (RIF1-RIF4) consisted of non-smoking subjects aged 31, 33, 25, and 29 years, with BMIs of 22.18, 24.47, 21.64, and 20.35 kg/m². The CTR group reported no previous embryo transfers. In the RIF group, RIF1, RIF3, and RIF4 had undergone 3 prior transfers of good-quality embryos, while RIF2 had experienced 5. Regarding obstetric history, CTR1 and CTR2 were primiparous, while CTR3 and CTR4 were multiparous. All RIF subjects were nulliparous. All participants were confirmed free of uterine pathologies (including endometriosis and adenomyosis), endocrine, metabolic, auto-immune diseases and infection. Endometrial samples were collected via Pipelle biopsy from the uterine fundus and upper cavity at 7 days after the Luteinizing Hormone (LH) surge (LH + 7).
